content.comment_body: Hello, I have a [product_name] base module [article_no] and want to add an analog input expansion module. I've purchased [article_no] expansion module. The base module has 3 mechanical coding sockets, while the expansion module has 2 mechanical coding pins, so I can't connect them. According to the manual, the mechanical encoding pins prevent devices of different voltage classes from connecting. How can I expand my base module with an analog input module? Thanks, [user_name]

That's unfortunate. The new [product_name] with version [article_no] requires expansion units [article_no]. The [article_no] and [article_no] expansion units are only compatible with [product_name] up until version [article_no].
Thank you for your assistance. I will purchase [article_no] next. I hope I can connect and expand it directly to the base processor without needing an additional module or connector. Thanks.

analysis.insight_summary: The user tried to add an analog input expansion module to a [product_name] base module but found that mechanical coding made the modules incompatible. Forum members explained version-specific compatibility, narrowing down compatible expansion modules and uncovering confusion around product versioning.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wants to conveniently expand the base module with an analog input module, connecting it directly and without needing extra components or facing compatibility obstacles.
